newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FORECAST-North full year called lower.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FORECAST-North full year called lower.

text.p: Forestry products, minerals and mining equipment group North Ltd is tipped to post a fall in profit for the year ended June 30 when it releases its results to the market on Monday.

North, which warned in May its 1995/96 results would be hit by lower-than expected earnings from three key units -- North Forest Products, Robe River iron ore and Northparkes copper-gold -- was seen reporting an 18.3 percent decline in its pre-abnormals net profit.

Analysts are forecasting an average bottom line figure of A$101.5 million but many said it might be higher than expectations due to solid fourth quarter results from North's uranium unit, Energy Resources of Australia Ltd.

"The key driver there is just the (higher) price of uranium and the fact that they're not trading other people's uranium. They have much higher production and they're getting much better prices so it's a very good story there," one analyst said.
North's share of ERA's 1995/96 earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) was A$60.8 million, up from A$39.1 million a year earlier.
Analysts have forecast a average 27 percent slide in EBIT for North's Forest Products unit to A$34.1 million.
They blamed the weakness mainly on lower woodchip volumes stemming from government restrictions on the company's woodchip export licences which were eventually removed in January.
"It will probably take forestry a couple of years to recover," another analyst predicted.

Iron ore EBIT from the Robe River operations in Western Australia were on average seen falling slightly to around A$111 million with higher production failing to translate to higher shipments, analysts said.
"They have higher operating costs because of exploration costs and other things so they are facing margin pressure (at Robe River)," one noted.
Gold EBIT from the Kanowna Belle and Peak Hill mines were, on average, expected to come in at A$33 million, up from A$20.6 million a year ago on increased production and lower costs.
The Northparkes mine was dogged by commissioning problems during the year which were likely to have dragged EBIT contribution from the mine lower, analysts said.

Six months of zinc production from the Swedish Zincgruvan mine, the purchase of which was finalised in November, were unlikely to contribute a significant amount to group earnings due to falling zinc prices and lower than average head grades.
Interest costs were forecast to rise because of a reduction in cash on deposit.
"(The interest cost rise) is just after they invested the cash in the Zincgruvan project and Bajo de Alumbrera (copper-gold mine in Argentina)," an analyst said.
Warman mining equipment earnings were seen static at around A$36 million. -- Melbourne bureau 61-3 9286-1435
